item.title: 'Just need to clear something up': Kevin Pietersen on why he didn't travel to Pakistan with England cricket team
item.description: Former England cricketer Kevin Pietersen has explained why he was absent from England latest white-ball assignment in Pakistan, clarifying that his role with the national team is that of a consultant rather than a full-time employee. His absence had attracted attention after he was spotted in Delhi attending the India Championship golf tournament while England were playing in Pakistan. Pietersen, who joined England's white-ball coaching setup earlier this year as a specialist mentor, said his responsibilities do not require him to travel with the team for every series or tournament. Taking to X on Saturday, Pietersen addressed the questions surrounding his absence and explained his position within the England setup. “Just need to clear something up once and for all. I am a consultant to the England Cricket Team," Pietersen tweeted on Saturday afternoon. He also clarified that he is not a permanent employee of the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) and will not accompany the team on every assignment over the coming year. — KP24 (@KP24) Pietersen's mentoring stint until 2027 ODI World Cup Pietersen was appointed as a mentor for England's white-ball teams, with his contract running until the 2027 ODI World Cup, which will be jointly hosted by South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe. He is part of a coaching group that includes Marcus Trescothick, Tim Southee, Jeetan Patel and Sarah Taylor, with Brendon McCullum serving as the white-ball head coach. The former England batter returned to the national setup around 12 years after his international career ended following the 2013-14 Ashes series. His first assignment as a mentor came during England's white-ball series against Sri Lanka earlier this year.

item.title: Pritchard’s 30 Points Expose Bulls’ Fatal Turnover Flaw
item.description: David Butler II-Imagn Images After losing by 35 points on Monday, they did it again on Friday, turning the ball over 16 times in a 125-111 loss to the Boston Celtics. Payton Pritchard led the charge with 30 points, hitting 9 of 17 shots. He scored 20 of those points in the first half alone, setting a tone that the Bulls could never shake. The Celtics pulled away to a 32-point lead with just under two minutes left in the first half, Chicago began to close the gap in the third quarter, according to CelticsBlog. A Paint Dominance That Broke Chicago Boston didn’t just win; they controlled the interior. The team scored 56 points in the paint, a number that highlights their physical dominance over the Bulls. Per the Associated Press, the Celtics converted 21 of their points directly off those 16 turnovers. Jayson Tatum added 26 points in 34 minutes, while Paul George contributed 18 points and eight assists. The starters did their damage early. Chicago shot just 38 percent from the field and 30 percent from three-point range, unable to find a rhythm against a defense that forced mistakes. The Turnover Cycle Continues Chicago has now lost four straight games, and the ball handling is the root cause. On Monday, they turned the ball over 25 times, leading to 39 Celtics points. On Friday, they reduced that number to 16, but the result was the same: Boston scored 21 points off those turnovers. Caleb Wilson was the bright spot for Chicago with 23 points. Norman Powell finished with 16, and Matas Buzelis added 14. Despite these efforts, the team could not stop Boston’s attack. The Celtics have now won four games in a row as NBA Cup group play continues. What Comes Next for Both Teams In Eastern Conference Group C, the Celtics and Bulls face each other, with point differential serving as the tiebreaker. Boston entered Friday with a +14 differential, while the Washington Wizards held +16. Every point matters now that the group play has begun. The Wizards and Celtics are tied for the lead with a 1-0 record. Looking ahead, the Bulls travel to Philadelphia on Monday. The Celtics head to Orlando on Sunday. Pritchard’s performance against the Bulls on Oct. 26 was also strong, as he scored 28 points in just 22 minutes. That history suggests he has a specific knack for this matchup. The Celtics and Wizards are tied at the top of their group.

item.title: Matos moves aside to give players the plaudits
item.description: Vitor Matos will celebrate a year in charge at Swansea next month [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Vitor Matos says he wanted Swansea City's players to take the plaudits after leaving them to savour the moment after an emphatic victory over Blackburn Rovers. Swansea bounced back from their shock 5-0 loss at Queens Park Rangers last weekend by handing out a thrashing of their own at the Swansea.com Stadium. Stephen Eustaquio, Joseph Opoku, Filip Lissah and Ross Stewart all found the target as Swansea thumped an in-form Blackburn side 4-0. After the game, Matos acknowledged the home crowd before swiftly heading down the tunnel rather than celebrating as he normally does in front of the East Stand. The Swansea head coach explained that it was a deliberate attempt to ensure his team took the credit for their biggest win of the season. "I think after last week, more than for me, this was for them," Matos said. Stylish Swansea romp to victory over Blackburn "They needed to have that feeling. They needed to have that moment. "The responsibility is always mine when we don't win, but when we win, they need to get that feeling, and that's what I wanted: for them to have the connection with the fans." Questions had been asked of Swansea after the Rangers mauling, which came on the back of a home defeat to West Ham United. But they responded in emphatic fashion by dismantling a Blackburn side who arrived in Wales on the back of four wins in their previous six games. "We have a lot of players with really good character, a lot of players with a squad full of really good human beings," Matos added. "I think that's the most important thing for us, to have these types of players who really care about where they are, really care about the team, really care about each other, really care about the club. "That's what we try to build, and when you have this kind of answer after what happened last week, you can see that." Swansea, who are second in the table after leaders Middlesbrough beat Charlton , are back in action at Portsmouth on Tuesday. The Swans will assess the fitness of Eustaquio, one of several standout performers against Blackburn, who left the pitch late on complaining of a groin issue. Matos will hope to have Marko Stamenic back in his squad at Fratton Park after the New Zealand international missed out against Rovers because of a virus. item.description: Canelo Alvarez will return to the ring this evening, challenging Christian Mbilli for the WBC super-middleweight title in Riyadh . Although the Saudi city has been the target of deadly attacks in recent weeks , Canelo has arrived ahead of his first fight in 13 months , after he was outpointed by fellow great Terence Crawford in Las Vegas. • FOLLOW LIVE: All the build-up to Canelo vs Mbilli Against Mbilli, the 36-year-old Canelo faces a stern task; the Cameroonian is the younger man, at 31, and he enters his first title defence with an unbeaten record. Canelo Alvarez (right) at the weigh-in for his fight with Terence Crawford (Getty) Last time out, on the Canelo vs Crawford undercard, Mbilli fought Lester Martinez to a brutal draw to retain the interim WBC title, but he was later upgraded to regular champion when Crawford retired. Can Canelo prove that he is still among the best in the world? Or, as he returns from elbow surgery, will he show himself to be in the twilight of his great career? Here’s all you need to know. When is the fight? Canelo vs Mbilli will take place on Saturday 31 October at the ANB Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The main card is expected to begin at 4pm GMT (9am PT / 11am CT / 12pm ET), with main-event ring walks following at 8.30pm GMT (1.30pm PT / 3.30pm CT / 4.30pm ET). How can I watch it? The event will stream live exclusively on DAZN pay-per-view at a cost of £24.99 ($79.99 in the US), and on DAZN Ultimate Tier – which is priced at £24.99 per month. You can purchase the fight or an Ultimate Tier subscription here. Will the event go ahead, and why is this a question? The organisation of this fight card had been the subject of intense speculation in recent weeks, due to numerous deadly attacks on Riyadh’s airports. Per Saudi authorities, more than 300 people have been left injured and at least 21 dead, due to strikes by the Yemen-aligned Houthis. The international airport was reopened, but the US Department of State urged citizens to “reconsider travel to Saudi Arabia due to risk of drone and missile targeting”, while areas near the Yemen border were listed as such: “do not travel due to terrorism”. A large plume of black smoke rises from the fuel storage area at King Khalid International Airport (Reuters) Despite these attacks, Saudi adviser and boxing matchmaker Turki Alalshikh continued to promote the fight, and he tweeted earlier this month , “[Canelo] fears nothing,” adding: “My country is home to the two Holy Mosques, land of peace, safety, rich civilisation, deep history and kind-hearted people.” Canelo arrived in Riyadh on Monday and said in a video on Alalshikh’s X account: “I love to be here in Riyadh, and I’m excited to fight on Saturday.” However, one undercard bout was cancelled, as first reported by journalist Dan Rafael , who said Lindolfo Delgado would “probably not” face Arthur Biyarslanov; Delgado and his team had reportedly not made travel plans, although Biyarslanov had already arrived in Riyadh. item.title: Cowboys’ Worst Rush Defense Meets Love’s Return In Sunday Clash
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys have allowed over 1,000 rushing yards this season, a stat that should scare any fan heading into Sunday. Now comes the most dangerous running back in the league, Jeremiyah Love, right when the defense looks most vulnerable. Seth Cox at Revenge of the Birds reported that Love will play against the Cowboys after missing time with an ankle injury. This timing creates a perfect storm for a game that could define the season for both teams. Love was the third overall pick in the 2026 draft and brings elite speed and receiving skills to the field. Despite missing their last few games, he has already led the Arizona Cardinals backfield in fantasy scoring. The Cowboys defense has struggled to stop the run all year, giving up an average of 4.7 yards per carry. That number looks even worse when you see Love lining up against a fourth-string right guard who might be pushed to the center spot. A History of Pain for Dallas Forget the current record for a second and look at the history. The Cowboys have not beaten the Cardinals since 2017, a dry spell that feels like an eternity in Arlington. Sean Martin at Blogging The Boys noted that without that one win in 2017, Arizona would hold an active nine-game winning streak against Dallas. The last time these teams met, the Cowboys won 28-17., and they are desperate to avoid a sixth loss to the same opponent. Because the Cowboys have already dropped games they were supposed to win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and New York Giants, the stakes are high. If they lose this one, the season could get messy fast. The Cardinals are 2-5 but just beat the Los Angeles Rams 18-16 in a legitimate upset. The Edge Must Be Set Defense coach Christian Parker showed new looks against the Eagles, but the run defense still had a hard time setting the edge. That specific failure against the run is what the Cardinals will try to exploit on Sunday. John Laghezza at FantasyLife pointed out that the Cowboys rank bottom-5 in several key pass defense stats, but the real story is the ground game. Arizona ranks 25th in 3rd and short conversion rate, which is the ultimate drive killer, but Love changes that math. Love averages right at 3.7 yards per carry, which matches the team average, but he is the spark the offense needs. The Cowboys need to stop the run first or they will face a long day against a quarterback who keeps his job by alternating great and bad games. For a six-week span, Jacoby Brissett has pattern-matched alternating QB1 and QB2 performances now, making him a tough matchup for any defense. With Matt Eberflus leading in 2025, the Sunday afternoon matchup is a crucial redemption opportunity for a defense that failed to establish an edge versus Jacoby Brissett and these Cardinals. If the Cowboys cannot fix their run defense against a team with a top-tier rookie back, they will face another loss that feels a lot like the one from last year. item.title: Chiefs Must Trade Worthy For Thomas To Fix Deep Passing
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs have a clear problem on the outside. They need a big target who can win the long ball. The Seattle Seahawks exposed this flaw last Sunday. The Seahawks’ defense took away the Chiefs’ run game and none of Kansas City’s receivers could create separation, Nguyen wrote. This loss showed the team needs a change before the November 10 deadline. Fox Sports’ Steven Ruiz laid out a bold plan to fix it. To acquire Jacksonville Jaguars wideout Brian Thomas Jr., he suggested a direct trade. Statistics and contract details support this reasoning. The Size Problem Mahomes Faces The Chiefs have chased the ghost of Tyreek Hill for too long. They brought in a bunch of undersized speedsters who cannot win 50/50 balls. Someone capable of battling for the ball amidst traffic is required by Patrick Mahomes. Xavier Worthy leads the receiving corps lately, but his stats show a struggle. Across six contests, he recorded only 24 catches totaling 217 yards. No season has seen him surpass the 700 receiving yards mark. Thomas offers the size they lack. In his 2024 rookie campaign, he tallied 87 receptions, 1,282 yards, and 10 touchdowns. Thomas was recently benched by the Jaguars since the offense utilizes him sparingly. This creates a chance for a fresh start. A Swap That Makes Financial Sense The money works for both sides in this deal. A four-year, $14.6 million rookie pact signed by Thomas extends through the 2027 season. Worthy holds a comparable four-year, $13.7 million agreement expiring in 2027. The financial pieces fit together neatly. Ruiz noted that “Both the Chiefs and Jaguars are reportedly interested in adding a receiver at the deadline, and both want one who can help in the deep passing game.” He called it “the most off-the-wall trade proposal of the bunch, but this swap makes a lot of sense on paper.”Neither athlete has completely fulfilled expectations so far, though both displayed moments of brilliance. While shifting environments doesn’t guarantee improvement, altering one’s role frequently helps. The Deadline Looms for Kansas City The window to make a move closes on November 10. With Tyquan Thornton sidelined for the year, the team lacks depth at that spot. Other options like Josh Downs or Marquise Brown are being discussed by insiders. The Athletic’s Ted Nguyen predicted the Chiefs will land Josh Downs for a fourth-round pick. According to reports, multiple clubs have already expressed interest in Downs. However, the Worthy for Thomas swap addresses the size issue directly. It gives two young first-round picks a new role. The Chiefs need to act fast to stay in the Super Bowl hunt. The next game is Sunday, Nov. 1, at Empower Field at Mile High against the Denver Broncos.

item.title: Five cross country teams claim regional titles; 9 teams, 8 individuals qualify for state
item.description: It was a banner day for Holland-area runners at regional championships around West Michigan on Halloween. Five teams won regional championships, four other teams qualified for state, with three missing by one spot, and eight individuals also qualified as nine of the area's 10 schools will be represented at the state finals on Nov. 7 at Michigan International Speedway. In all, a stunning 62 Holland-area runners will be competing at the state finals. Holland Christian won the boys and girls Division 2 regional titles, Saugatuck won the boys and girls Division 3 regional titles and Holland Calvary won the boys Division 4 regional title. The Holland High School and Black River boys and girls qualified as teams for the state finals and the Zeeland West boys and girls and Fennville boys missed joining them by one spot. Individually, Zeeland East's Adalyn Raab won the Division 1 regional and Saugatuck's Livia Curtis won the Division 3 regional. More: Saugatuck girls cross country back to state power behind 'pilot light' senior duo Here is a look at what happened in each region: DIVISION 2 Holland Christian wins regionals, Holland qualifies in boys and girls The Holland Christian girls cross country team scored 34 points to win the Division 2 regional. Holland scored 72 points to finish second and also qualify for state. Holland Christian was led by a second-place finish by Avery Engbers (18:00.6). item.title: Why Penn State football will miss top two players vs Purdue in Big Ten
item.description: STATE COLLEGE — Penn State football will have to break its four-game losing streak without just one but two of its top playmakers. For sure, its two best receivers. Sophomore Koby Howard will miss his fifth straight game here Saturday against the Purdue Boilermakers with an undisclosed injury − and now he'll be joined by senior wideout Chase Sowell, according to the Big Ten's pregame availability report . The two Nittany Lions will be the biggest misses for their critical recovery attempt in Beaver Stadium against the struggling but dangerous and motivated Purdue team. While the Lions will miss more than a dozen players for this game, losing Howard and Sowell are a major concern considering the lack of proven depth at receiver − and the need to excel in the pass game. The Boilermakers feature one of the worst-rated pass defenses in the nation, and PSU's scuffling offense and quarterback Rocco Becht must be able to take advantage. The Lions hope for the return of backup linebacker Cam Smith and the addition of former safety Marcus Neal, Jr. to boost the thinnest position on the team. PSU was down to only three primary linebackers after the recent injury to promising sophomore Alex Tatsch , who will miss the rest of the season. Sowell, who has emerged as the Lions’ top option in the pass game without Howard, just enjoyed an 11-catch, 151-yard performance in Penn State’s loss at Michigan. He battled through minor injuries the past two games. Will two of the Big Ten's top receivers be back for the road trip to Washington next weekend? For now, the Lions (3-4, 0-4 Big Ten) and Boilermakers (3-4, 2-2) desperately need a victory to help right their disappointing seasons and make a push to some kind of a postseason game. Lions who will be game-time decisions, according to the report: starting defensive end Yvan Kemajou, tight end Brian Kortovich and defensive tackle Amstrong Nnodim. Penn State's list of unavailable players for the Purdue game: Howard, Sowell, Tatsch, defensive ends Max Granville and Mason Robinson, offensive lineman Will Thompkins, cornerbacks Tyler Armstead, Josh Johnson and Christian Askew, defensive tackles Liam Andrews and Alijah Carnell, safety Omarion Davis, tight end Cooper Alexander and kickoff specialist Cristiano Rosa . Replays revealed he never looked at the ball, his focus entirely on Fofana, while Michael Carrick completely ignored Martinez as he headed down the tunnel. A man down and trailing by two, United faced an impossible comeback task as their winless run stretched to nine matches. Speaking after the final whistle, Schmeichel was hugely critical of Martinez, squarely blaming him for United’s loss. The Dane also accused Martinez of trying to orchestrate an exit. Schmeichel slams Martinez The iconic United goalkeeper said [as quoted by SportBible ], “I put this solely on Lisandro Martinez’s shoulders. This is an absolute disgrace how he played this game.” “Two weeks ago, he came out and made some very, very strong statements against his teammates, against the football club, and it felt like he was trying to orchestrate a move.” “He’s in the last year of his contract. What he did today, honestly, I have no words.” “The first goal, I mean, he’s played a World Cup final. Somebody who’s played a World Cup final can’t defend the way he defended on the first goal.” “The penalty… I have no words. I literally have no words for how crazy that was. And then he walks off the pitch, shaking his head as if he’s done nothing wrong. So bad.” United are next in action on Tuesday when they face AS Roma in the Champions League.
